children: Technology services industry in India will shift to intelligence arbitrage amidst the AI transformation, moving away from its earlier cost-focused global identity, as per Rahul Singh, Chief Operating Officer, HCL Technologies speaking at the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave.
Speaking at a panel discussion focused on the AI economy, Singh answered queries on how the services industry is adapting in the AI age.

“The Indian IT services industry has long been recognized for cost arbitrage and audit. It will shift to an intelligence arbitrage. It will be a momentous occasion for the country to catapult from being seen as a cost provider to an intelligence provider,” said Singh.

Speaking about the sector in the AI age, Singh stressed the pivot to an outcome-based model versus simply producing the technology. The transition takes time as companies evolve from input to output, change pricing models, renew client trust, in turn impacting the market.
“As the industry pivots, the markets will self-correct and we’ll heal over time,” he said.
When asked about jobs, Singh advised the youth to learn multiple disciplines. The industry will move up the curve as individuals become sharper and more skilled with AI.

“While the numerics may be different, may not be high growth rates, but the value addition will be much higher. The industry is moving to more higher quality of engineering work to be done. We are now developing a group who can create AI and who can use AI. Our students are very bright and sharp,” he said.

Professor V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras, stressed three job profiles in particular: AI auditor, where an individual audits and AI system for correctness, for responsibility, accountability, safety; AI integrators, who understand where AI can fit in and put workflows into perspective; interdiscplinary data analytics expert with subject-expertise.

The conversation also moved towards AI’s impact on overall human behaviour. Here, Nitin Bawankule, Head of Enterprise at OpenAI, argued that AI makes individuals smarter by bringing information and intelligence to everyone’s disposal.

“The fundamental difference is that human beings should evolve more towards critical thinking: asking the right kind of questions, evaluating the right outputs and applying your judgment,” said Bawankule.

title: ‘India’s ITeS industry will move to intelligence arbitrage from cost arbitrage’
